classification.difficultyReason: Reconstruct the trajectory from its range and maximum, convert the girl's height to metres, solve the resulting quadratic and select the descending-path root.

content.prompt:
The graph shows the trajectory of an AFL ball kicked by a Year 11 student.

The ball reaches a maximum height of 12 metres and hits the ground 40 metres from where it was kicked. As the ball is falling, it just passes over the head of a Year 7 girl who is 134 cm tall.

How far away was the Year 7 girl standing from where the ball was kicked?

Answer in metres rounded to 2 decimals.

spec.description: Unshaded trajectory from the origin to a positive horizontal intercept, with rightward x-axis and upward H-axis. No ticks, numerical labels, vertex marker or girl.
spec.mathematics: H=-3x(x-40)/100 for 0≤x≤40; the curve has maximum height 12 at x=20. Numerical features determine the curve but are not printed on this reference graph.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied reference curve; no answer annotations.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be the horizontal distance in metres and $H$ the height in metres. The ground intercepts are $0$ and $40$, so $H=cx(x-40)$. By symmetry, the maximum occurs at $x=20$.

$$\begin{align*}12&=c(20)(20-40)\\c&=-\frac{3}{100}\\H&=-\frac{3}{100}x(x-40)\end{align*}$$

The girl's height is $134\text{ cm}=1.34\text{ m}$.

$$\begin{align*}1.34&=-\frac{3}{100}x(x-40)\\134&=-3x^2+120x\\3x^2-120x+134&=0\\x&=\frac{120\pm\sqrt{(-120)^2-4(3)(134)}}{2(3)}\\x&=\frac{120\pm\sqrt{12792}}{6}\\x&\approx1.15\text{ or }38.85\end{align*}$$

The ball is falling when $x>20$, so the girl was standing $38.85\text{ m}$ from where the ball was kicked.
